guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: dirty blues-rock crunch with hard edge and raw slide grit
tone.profile: dirty blues-rock crunch with hard edge and raw slide grit
tone.summary: A gritty, overdriven signal chain using a classic UK amp model (UK 45/50) combined with a distortion pedal for bite, emphasizing thick lower mids and dry tone suitable for blues-rock slide work.

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - Bring It On Home - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide initial grit and bite for the raw blues-rock tone.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen to emulate a slightly dirty, mid-focused boost/overdrive suitable for early Marshall tones without being overly polished.

blocks.purpose: Add aggressive, raw grit and bite necessary for the 'hard edge' and slide grit.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style provides a mid-humped, dirty crunch that complements the Plexi/Marshall vibe without sounding modern or overly high-gain.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Plexi/early Marshall sound with thick lower mids and raw breakup.

alternatives.reason: A similar, but slightly different flavor of British amp.

blocks.purpose: Provide the desired 'dry close-mic feel' and classic British cabinet tone.
Boost the thick lower mids and cut harsh high frequencies to achieve a 'dirty blues-rock crunch'.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range sculpting than general tone controls.

blocks.purpose: Optional: Keep modulation off to maintain a dry, raw feel.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is included as an optional module but kept inactive to ensure the tone remains 'dry and rude'.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth without washing out the raw grit.
blocks.gap: A minimal delay is used to add dimension, keeping the focus on the core dirty tone.

alternatives.reason: Too much warmth might soften the 'hard edge'.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal sense of space without adding excessive polish or sparkle.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly to maintain the 'dry' feel while giving some depth.

alternatives.reason: Too bright and polished for this raw tone.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to enhance cabinet realism and capture the raw, dirty close-mic sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the perceived depth and grit of the cabinet tone for a more realistic close-mic feel.
